allyrion.summary:
House Allyrion of Godsgrace is a major Dornish noble house. Godsgrace sits near the confluence of the Scourge and the Vaith into the Greenblood.

Their blazon is a golden hand on gyronny red and black. Their words do not appear in the books, but according to semi-canon sources they are "No Foe May Pass".
facts: A golden hand on gyronny red and black, (Gyronny gules and sable, a hand or)

appleton.summary: House Appleton of Appleton is a noble house from Appleton in the Reach. According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with quarterly: An apple tree on yellow, a grey gatehouse on white. Their words are not known.
facts: Quarterly: An apple tree on yellow, a grey gatehouse on white, (Quarterly clockwise, 1st and 3rd or, an apple tree proper, 2nd and 4th argent, a gatehouse cendrée)

arryn.summary:
House Arryn of the Eyrie is one of the Great Houses of Westeros, and is the principal noble house in the Vale of Arryn. Their main seat is the Eyrie, which is considered impregnable. House Arryn has at least one other holding, their winter castle at the Gates of the Moon, which was once their main seat. Both of these fortifications sit astride the Giant's Lance, the tallest mountain in the Vale, the Gates of the Moon at its foot, the Eyrie at its top.

The Arryn sigil is a sky-blue falcon soaring upwards, outlined against a white moon on a sky-blue field, and their words are "As High as Honor".

The Arryns of the Eyrie have a collection of distant relatives located throughout the Vale. Although they are much poorer than the ruling Arryns, aside from the Arryns of Gulltown, these lesser branches are described by Petyr Baelish as proud due to their name and heritage.
facts: A sky-blue falcon soaring against a white moon, on sky-blue, (Bleu celeste, upon a plate a falcon rousant of the field)
King of Mountain and Vale (pre-Conquest), Lord of the Eyrie, Defender of the Vale, Warden of the East
House Arryn of Gulltown, Other branches in the Vale

arryn-of-gulltown.summary: House Arryn of Gulltown is a small cadet branch of House Arryn located in the city of Gulltown. They chose to marry merchants in Gulltown, making them richer than most of their cousins. However they are considered uncouth, and so they are not discussed by the rest of the family. Although their coat of arms does not officially appear in the books, Isembard Arryn, the head of the house during king Aegon III Targaryen's regency, was said to have the falcon on his sigil painted in gold, which means that their arms are the same as their cousins from the Eyrie.
facts: A sky-blue falcon soaring against a white moon, on a sky-blue field, (Bleu celeste, upon a plate a falcon rousant of the field)

ashford.summary: House Ashford of Ashford is a noble house from Ashford in the Reach. It blazons its arms with a white sun-and-chevron on orange. According to semi-canon sources, their words are "Our Sun Shines Bright".
facts: A white sun-and-chevron on orange, (Tenné, beneath a chevron inverted a sun-in-splendour argent)

baelish.summary:
House Baelish is a noble house from the Vale of Arryn. Their seat is an unnamed, old flint tower, which commands no more than a few stony acres on the smallest of the Fingers. House Baelish's smallfolk consists of a village of a dozen families in huts of piled stone beside a peat bog.

The current lord, Petyr Baelish, is only the second generation of the landed family. His grandfather had been a landless hedge knight, and his father the smallest of lords. While the traditional arms of House Baelish depict the Titan's head, Petyr has adopted as new arms a field of silver mockingbirds on green.
facts: Lord of Harrenhal, Lord Paramount of the Trident
A hedge knight of Braavosi descent

banefort.summary:
House Banefort of Banefort is a noble house from Banefort in the westerlands, one of the main families sworn to Casterly Rock.

According to semi-canon sources, they blazon their shields with a hooded man, black on grey with within a fiery tressure.
facts: A hooded man, black on grey, within a fiery tressure, (Cendrée, a hooded man sable within a tressure rayonné along the outer edge gules)

baratheon.summary:
House Baratheon of Storm's End is one of the Great Houses of Westeros, and is the principal house in the stormlands, which they rule as Lords Paramount of the Stormlands. Their seat, Storm's End, is an ancient castle raised by the Storm Kings from the now-extinct House Durrandon. The Baratheon sigil is a crowned black stag on a field of gold, and their words are "Ours is the Fury".

After Robert's Rebellion, House Baratheon split into three branches. Lord Robert Baratheon was crowned King of the Andals, the Rhoynar, and the First Men and took up residence at the Red Keep, thereby creating House Baratheon of King's Landing. With House Targaryen now in exile, Robert gave their castle of Dragonstone to his younger brother, Stannis, creating House Baratheon of Dragonstone. Robert's youngest brother, Renly, replaced him as the Lord of Storm's End, continuing House Baratheon of Storm's End.
facts: A crowned stag black on a golden field, (Or, a stag crowned sable)
Lord of Storm's End, Lord Paramount of the Stormlands
House Baratheon of King's Landing, House Baratheon of Dragonstone

baratheon-of-dragonstone.summary: House Baratheon of Dragonstone is a branch of House Baratheon of Storm's End. Their seat is Dragonstone, the island castle that sits off the mainland to the northeast of King's Landing, and the Great House commands the allegiance of the lords of the narrow sea. Their founder and current head is Lord Stannis Baratheon, who seized the island at the end of Robert's Rebellion and received it as a reward from his brother, King Robert I Baratheon.
facts: Lord of Dragonstone, Lord of Storm's End (disputed), King of Westeros (disputed)

baratheon-of-king-s-landing.summary: House Baratheon of King's Landing is the royal line of House Baratheon of Storm's End, from which it comes. The Great House receives the support of the mainland houses from the crownlands.
facts: King of the Andals, the Rhoynar, and the First Men, Lord of the Seven Kingdoms, Lord of Storm's End (disputed)

bar-emmon.summary:
House Bar Emmon of Sharp Point is a noble house from Sharp Point in the crownlands. They are sworn to Dragonstone.

Their blazon is a leaping blue swordfish on fretty silver on white.
facts: A leaping blue swordfish on fretty silver on white, (White fretty silver, a swordfish embowed azure)

beesbury.summary:
House Beesbury of Honeyholt is a minor noble house from the Reach, sworn to the Hightowers. Honeyholt is located next to the Honeywine river, which flows towards Oldtown and the Whispering Sound.

Their arms are three yellow beehives on a black pale over a paly black and yellow field. Their words do not appear in the books, but according to semi-canon sources it is "Beware our Sting".
facts: Three yellow beehives on a black pale on a field paly black and yellow, (Paly or and sable, on a pale of the last three beehives of the first)

belmore.summary: House Belmore of Strongsong is a noble house from Strongsong in the Vale of Arryn. They are one of the more powerful noble houses sworn to House Arryn. The Belmore arms are six silver bells on purple, 3-2-1. Their words do not appear in the books.
facts: Six silver bells on purple, 3-2-1, (Purpure, six bells 3-2-1 argent)
Before the coming of the Andals

blackbar.summary: House Blackbar of Bandallon is a noble house from Bandallon in the Reach. According to semi-canon sources, the Blackbars blazon their shields with a black fess on silver.
facts: A black fess on silver, (Argent, a fess sable)

blackmont.summary:
House Blackmont of Blackmont is a major Dornish noble house. Their seat, Blackmont, is on the banks of the Torrentine in the Red Mountains of Dorne.

Their blazon is a black vulture with a pink infant in its claws on yellow. Their words do not appear in the books.
facts: A black vulture with a pink infant in its claws on yellow, (Or, a vulture sable clutching an infant carnation)

blackwood.summary:
House Blackwood of Raventree Hall is an old house from Raventree Hall in the riverlands, one of the main families sworn to House Tully of Riverrun. They once ruled the riverlands as kings during the Age of Heroes. They blazon their arms with a flock of ravens on scarlet surrounding a dead weirwood upon a black escutcheon. Their words have not yet been revealed by George R. R. Martin. House Blackwood rules over wider domains and can field a much larger army than their overlord of House Tully.

Raventree is located in Blackwood Vale north of Riverrun and the Red Fork.
facts: A flock of ravens on scarlet surrounding a dead weirwood upon a black escutcheon, (Gules, on an escutcheon sable a dead weirwood tree proper, all within an orle of ravens sable)
Lord of Raventree Hall, River king (historical)

bolton.summary:
House Bolton of the Dreadfort is a noble house from the Dreadfort in the north. They are an old line descended from the First Men and dating back to the Age of Heroes.

The Bolton sigil is a red flayed man, on pale pink spotted with red blood drops. According to George R. R. Martin, their words are "Our Blades Are Sharp". According to the Bolton servant "Reek", Lord Roose Bolton believes "a naked man has few secrets, but a flayed man has none".
facts: A red flayed man on pink de sang, (Carnation gouttée-de-sang, a flayed man gules)
Red King (historical), Lord of the Dreadfort, Warden of the North

bolton-of-winterfell.summary: House Bolton of Winterfell is a new noble house in the north, and a cadet branch of House Bolton of the Dreadfort.
facts: A red flayed man on pink de sang
Lord of Winterfell, Lord of the Hornwood

borrell.summary:
House Borrell of Sweetsister is a noble house from the Vale ruling over Sweetsister, an island of the Three Sisters, and its port town, Sisterton. Their castle is Breakwater in Sisterton. House Borrell's titles include Lord of Sweetsister, Shield of Sisterton, Master of Breakwater Castle, and Keeper of the Night Lamp. They are sworn to House Sunderland, who also reside in Sisterton.

Their arms are a white spider crab on grey-green. Their words do not appear in the books.
facts: A white spider crab on grey-green, (Vert-cendrée, a spider crab argent)
Lord of Sweetsister, Keeper of the Night Lamp, Shield of Sisterton, Master of Breakwater Castle

botley.summary:
House Botley of Lordsport is a noble house from the Iron Islands, one of the principal houses sworn to the Greyjoys. Their seat of Lordsport is located on the island of Pyke, at the opposite side of the Greyjoys' keep of Pyke.

Their blazon is a shoal of silver fish on pale green. Their words do not appear in the books.
facts: A shoal of silver fish on pale green, (Vert semé of fishes argent)
Balon Botley under Germund, Symond Botley under Tristifer

bracken.summary:
House Bracken of Stone Hedge is an old house from Stone Hedge in the riverlands, one of the main families sworn to House Tully of Riverrun. They blazon their arms with a red stallion upon a golden escutcheon on brown. Their words do not appear in the books.

The Bracken lands lie along the Red Fork of the Trident. They rule over wider domains and can field a much larger army than their overlord of House Tully.
facts: A red stallion upon a golden escutcheon on brown, (Brunâtre, on an escutcheon or a stallion rampant gules)
Lord of the Stone Hedge, River king (historical)

brax.summary:
House Brax of Hornvale is a noble house from the westerlands, among the chief bannermen of House Lannister of Casterly Rock. Their seat is Hornvale.

Their shield depicts a purple unicorn on silver. Their motto has not been revealed yet.
facts: A purple unicorn on silver, (Argent, a unicorn purpure)

brune-of-brownhollow.summary:
House Brune of Brownhollow is a house of landed knights from Brownhollow, which is located in Crackclaw Point in the crownlands. According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with a bear paw, brown on white, within a double tressure brown. Their words are not known.

The Brunes of Brownhollow are cousins to the Brunes of the Dyre Den. Archmaester Gyldayn considers the Brunes of Crackclaw to be half-wild.
facts: A bear paw, brown on white, within a double tressure brown, (Argent, a bear's paw brunâtre within a double tressure of the last)

buckler.summary:
House Buckler of Bronzegate is a noble house from Bronzegate in the stormlands sworn to Storm's End.

According to semi-canon sources their arms depict three brass buckles on blue. Their motto is unknown.
facts: Three brass buckles on blue, (Azure, three buckles or)

buckwell.summary: House Buckwell of the Antlers is a noble house from Antlers in the crownlands. They are sworn to the Iron Throne. According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with a rack of golden antlers on vair. Their words are "Pride and Purpose".
facts: A rack of golden antlers on vair, (Vair, a stag's attire or)

bulwer.summary:
House Bulwer of Blackcrown is a noble house from the Reach, sworn to the Hightowers of Oldtown. Blackcrown is located on the northern coast of Whispering Sound.

According to semi-canon sources, the Bulwer arms depict a bull's skull, bone over blood. Their words do not appear in the books, but according to semi-canon sources they are Death Before Disgrace.
facts: A bull's skull, bone on blood, (Sanguine, a bull's skull argent)

burley.summary:
House Burley is a noble house from the north. It is one of the northern mountain clans. According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with a white knife in a blue pile on white.

It is unknown which part of the northern mountains they inhabit, however given their sigil depicts a white knife, their lands may be located about Long Lake, which is the source of the White Knife.
facts: A white knife in a blue pile on white, (Argent, on a pile azure a knife of the field)

butterwell.summary:
House Butterwell is a noble house of the riverlands. Their blazon is undy green, white, and yellow.

House Butterwell was once a rich house with extensive lands, though its main incomes came from dairy cows, prompting some to dismiss their origins as little more than upjumped cattle thieves, and once had a castle called Whitewalls. Lord Ambrose Butterwell was said to have had the best wines outside of the Arbor.
facts: Undy green, white, and yellow, (Barry wavy vert, argent, and or)

cafferen.summary: House Cafferen of Fawnton is a noble house from Fawnton in the stormlands, sworn to House Baratheon of Storm's End. They blazon their arms with two white fawns counter salient on green.
facts: Two white fawns counter salient on green, (Vert, two fawns counter-salient argent)

caron.summary:
House Caron of Nightsong is one of the principal noble houses in the stormlands, sworn to Storm's End. They rule from Nightsong and hold the title Lord of the Marches, although they do not hold dominion over other marcher lords in the Dornish Marches.

Their blazon is a field of black nightingales on yellow. Their words do not appear in the books, but according to semi-canon correspondence it is No Song so Sweet.
facts: A field of black nightingales on yellow, (Or, semé of nightingales sable)
Lord of Nightsong, Lord of the Marches

caswell.summary: House Caswell of Bitterbridge is a noble house from the Reach. Their seat is Bitterbridge, where the Roseroad meets the river Mander. Their blazon is a yellow centaur with bow on white. The Caswells carry the title Defender of the Fords.
facts: A yellow centaur with bow on white, (Argent, a centaur with bow or)
Lord of Bitterbridge, Defender of the Fords

celtigar.summary:
House Celtigar of Claw Isle rules Claw Isle, an island in the narrow sea off the coast of Crackclaw Point. The Celtigars are historically sworn to Dragonstone within the crownlands.

Their arms depict red crabs strewn on white. Their words do not appear in the books.
facts: Red crabs strewn on white, (Argent, semé of crabs gules)

cerwyn.summary:
House Cerwyn of Cerwyn is a noble house from the north. They are one of the closest bannermen to the Starks, Castle Cerwyn being just a half day's ride from Winterfell, and are among the most powerful as well.

Their blazon is a black battle-axe on silver. Their words do not appear in the books, but according to semi-canon sources, they are "Honed and Ready".
facts: A black battle-axe on silver, (Argent, a battle-axe sable)

chester.summary:
House Chester of Greenshield rules over Greenshield, one of the Shield Islands of the Reach.

According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with a green hand on a gold escutcheon on a green field, a border of red rayonne. Their words do not appear in the books.
facts: A green hand on a gold escutcheon on a green field, a border of red rayonne, (Vert, on an escutcheon or a hand of the field all within a bordure rayonny gules)

clegane.summary: House Clegane is a house of landed knights in the westerlands. They hold fealty to House Lannister of Casterly Rock, and are among their primary bannermen. Their lands are southeast of the Rock and include a towerhouse, which, according to a semi-canon source, is named Clegane's Keep. Their sigil depicts three dogs on a yellow field.
facts: Three black dogs running on yellow, (Or, three dogs courant sable)

coldwater.summary:
House Coldwater of Coldwater Burn is a noble house from Coldwater Burn in the Vale of Arryn. They are sworn to the Royces of Runestone.

According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with a blue pall with white borders on red. Their words do not appear in the books.
facts: A blue pall with white borders on red, (Gules, a pall azure, fimbriated argent)

connington.summary:
House Connington of Griffin's Roost is a house of landed knights from Griffin's Roost in the stormlands, sworn to Storm's End. It was formerly a lordly house whose lands once extended many leagues west, north, and south of Griffin's Roost, including reaching near to the rainwood.

Their blazon shows two griffins combatant counterchanged per pale on red and white. Their motto is unknown, though their traditional battle cry is A griffin! A griffin!
facts: Two griffins combatent countercharged on red and white, (Per pale gules and argent, two griffins combatant counterchanged)
Lord of Griffin's Roost, Knight of Griffin's Roost (post-Robert's Rebellion)

corbray.summary:
House Corbray of Heart's Home is a noble house from Heart's Home in the Vale of Arryn. It is an old but poor house. The ancestral Valyrian steel longsword of the Corbrays is Lady Forlorn.

They blazon their arms with three black ravens in flight holding three red hearts, on white. Their words do not appear in the books.
facts: Three black ravens in flight holding three red hearts, on white, (Argent, three ravens volant sable, each clutching in their claws a heart gules)
Lord of Heart's Home, Lord of the Five Fingers (historical), King of the Fingers (historical)

costayne.summary:
House Costayne of Three Towers is a noble house from Three Towers in the Reach, sworn to the Hightowers. Their castle is located on the southern coast of the Whispering Sound.

The Costaynes blazon their shield with quartered: a silver chalice on black, a black rose on yellow. Their words do not appear in the text.
facts: Quartered clockwise: a silver chalice on black, a black rose on yellow, (Quarterly, first and third sable, a chalice argent, second and fourth or, a rose of the first)

crakehall.summary:
House Crakehall of Crakehall is one of the primary noble houses from the westerlands. Their seat, Crakehall, is located along the Ocean Road between the Sunset Sea and a large forest.

Their arms depict a black and white brindled boar on brown. According to semi-canon sources their words are "None so Fierce".
facts: A black and white brindled boar on brown, (Brunâtre, a boar brindled sable and argent)
Lord of Crakehall, King of the Iron Islands (historical; briefly)

crane.summary:
House Crane of Red Lake is a noble house from Red Lake in the Reach. It is one of the principal houses sworn to House Tyrell.

They blazon their shield with a vee of golden cranes on pale blue.
facts: A vee of golden cranes on pale blue, (Bleu celeste, cranes in chevron inverted or)

crowl.summary: House Crowl of Deepdown is a noble house from Deepdown on the isle of Skagos in the north. According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with pily flame and black.
facts: Ply flame and black, (Pily gules and sable)

cuy.summary:
House Cuy of Sunhouse is a noble house from Sunhouse in the Reach, sworn to the Hightowers. Sunhouse is located by the town Cuy, along the coast southeast of Oldtown.

Neither their arms or their words appear in the text. According to semi-canon sources they blazon their shield as six yellow flowers on blue.

The Appendix for A Feast for Crows lists Branston Cuy with the title Lord of Sunflower Hall, but it has been confirmed that Sunhouse is the correct name for House Cuy's seat.
facts: Six yellow flowers on blue, (Azure, six flowers or)

dalt.summary:
House Dalt of Lemonwood is a house of landed knights from Dorne, and their head is known as the Knight of Lemonwood. Their seat of Lemonwood is located south of the mouth of the Greenblood, close to the shadow city of Sunspear.

Their arms are a purple field strewn with lemons. Their words do not appear in the books.
facts: Lemons strewn on purple, (Purpure, semé of lemons proper)

darry.summary: House Darry of Darry is a noble house from Castle Darry in the riverlands. Historically it had been one of the more prominent and powerful houses of the Trident, until the fall of the Targaryens in Robert's Rebellion. Their blazon is a black plowman on brown; the central building where the Darrys have their apartments is called the Plowman's Keep. Their words do not appear in the books.
facts: A black plowman on brown, (Brunâtre, a plowman sable)

dayne.summary:
House Dayne of Starfall is a noble house from Starfall in Dorne. They are among the principal houses sworn to House Martell. The Sword of the Morning is a title given to a Dayne knight who is considered worthy of wielding the greatsword Dawn, a blade said to be created from the heart of falling star.

The Daynes' blazon is a white sword and a falling star, crossing on a lavender background. Their words have not yet been published.

A lesser branch of the family are the Daynes of High Hermitage.
facts: A white sword and falling star crossed on lilac, (Purpure, a blazing star bendways surmounted by a sword bendways sinister argent)
Lord of Starfall, Sword of the Morning, King of the Torrentine (historical)

dondarrion.summary:
House Dondarrion of Blackhaven is an old house from Blackhaven in the stormlands, sworn to House Baratheon of Storm's End.

Blackhaven, the castle of these great marcher lords, is located in the Dornish Marches near the Boneway, controlling the pass to Dorne. Their sigil is a forked purple lightning bolt on a black field speckled with four-pointed stars. Their motto is unknown.
facts: Forked purple lightning on a black field speckled with 4-pointed stars, (Sable semé of mullets of four points argent, a lightning bolt forked purpure)

durrandon.summary: House Durrandon of Storm's End was the house of the Storm Kings from the stormlands. Their seat was Storm's End, an ancient castle raised by Durran Godsgrief, the founder of their line. The Durrandon sigil was a crowned black stag on a field of gold. Their words were Ours is the Fury. Both sigil and words were adopted by House Baratheon, who descend from House Durrandon through the female line, during Aegon's Conquest.
facts: A crowned stag black on a golden field, (Or, a stag crowned sable)

dustin.summary:
House Dustin of Barrowton is a noble house from the north, one of the major families sworn to House Stark. Their castle is Barrow Hall in Barrowton, a prominent town in the north. The current head of the house is Lady Barbrey Dustin, a Ryswell by birth.

Their arms portray two rusted longaxes with black shafts crossed, a black crown between their points, on yellow. The rusted crown on their arms derives from their claim of descent from the First King and the Barrow Kings that followed him.
facts: Two rusted longaxes with black shafts crossed, a black crown between their points, on yellow, (Or, two rusted longaxes in saltire proper, hafted sable, between the points a crown of the last)

elesham.summary: House Elesham of the Paps is a noble house from the Paps in the Vale. According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with a double pile inverted, stone on pink, a black mullet between.
facts: A double pile inverted, stone on pink, a black mullet between, (Rose, between two piles inverted cendrée a mullet sable)

errol.summary:
House Errol of Haystack Hall is a noble house from Haystack Hall in the stormlands, one of the principal houses sworn to House Baratheon.

Neither their arms or their words appear in the text. According to semi-canon sources they blazon their shield as a yellow haystack on orange.
facts: A yellow haystack on orange, (Tenné, a haystack or)

estermont.summary:
House Estermont of Greenstone is a noble house from Greenstone in the stormlands and is one of the principal houses sworn to House Baratheon of Storm's End. They rule the small island of Estermont east of Cape Wrath.

Their arms depict a dark green sea turtle on pale green. Their motto is unknown.
facts: A dark green sea turtle on pale green, (Vert, a sea-turtle of the field)

farman.summary:
House Farman of Faircastle is a noble house from Faircastle on Fair Isle, off the coast of the westerlands. They are sworn to House Lannister of Casterly Rock, and are considered among their principal bannermen. The Farmans are known for their hatred of the ironborn from the Iron Islands.

House Farman's words are The Wind Our Steed. They blazon their arms with three silver ships on blue, a border of crimson and gold.
facts: Three silver ships on blue, a border of crimson and gold, (Azure, three galleys argent within a bordure compony gules and or)
Lord of Fair Isle, King of Fair Isle (formerly)

farwynd-of-the-lonely-light.summary:
House Farwynd of the Lonely Light is a branch of House Farwynd from the Iron Islands. Their seat is the Lonely Light, the main island in a group of thirteen islets eight days sail to the northwest of Great Wyk. They blazon their arms with per fesse: below a black sea with crested line, a black longship, outlined against the setting sun, dark red on orange.

Another branch of the family, House Farwynd of Sealskin Point, holds lands on the westernmost shores of Great Wyk, including the namesake seat. Since the builder of the Lonely Light took the name Farwynd, his branch may be the senior branch of the Farwynds.

fell.summary:
House Fell of Felwood is a noble house sworn to Storm's End. Their seat is Felwood in the northern stormlands.

Neither their arms or their words appear in the books, but according to semi-canon sources their arms are blazoned per fess, a white crescent moon in the first on black above a green field, a sprucetree line between.
facts: Per fess, a white crescent moon in the first on black above a green field, a sprucetree line between, (Per fess sapiné sable and vert, in canton an increscent argent)

fenn.summary:
House Fenn is a noble house from the north. They are crannogmen who live in the Neck.

According to semi-canon sources, House Fenn blazons their arms with three black water lilies, on pale violet.
facts: 3 black water lilies, on pale violet, (Purpure, three water lilies sable)

flint-of-flint-s-finger.summary:
House Flint of Flint's Finger is a noble house from Flint's Finger in the southwest of the north. According to a semi-canon source, they are probably less powerful than the Flints of Widow's Watch.

Their arms have been referred to as "the stone hand of House Flint of Flint's Finger", but no full description of their arms nor their words appear in the text. According to a semi-canon source, they blazon their banner as a grey stone hand upon a white inverted pall on paly black and grey.
facts: A grey stone hand upon a white inverted pall on paly black and grey, (Paly sable and cendrée on a pall inverted argent a hand couped of the second)

flint-of-widow-s-watch.summary:
House Flint of Widow's Watch is a noble house from Widow's Watch in the east of the north. They are probably the most powerful branch of House Flint, though the Flints of the mountains claim to be the oldest of the Flints.

Neither their arms or their words appear in the text. A semi-canon source blazons their banner as a blue field strewn with whitecaps, on a yellow chief with crested line a pair of blue eyes and gives their motto as "Ever Vigilant".
facts: A blue field strewn with whitecaps, on a yellow chief with crested line a pair of blue eyes, (Azure semé of whitecaps argent, on a chief wavy crested or two orbs of the second irised of the first and pupiled sable)
House Flint of Flint's Finger, House Flint of the mountains

florent.summary:
House Florent of Brightwater Keep is a noble house from Brightwater Keep in the Reach, one of the main houses sworn to House Tyrell of Highgarden. Their sigil is a red fox's head encircled by blue flowers on ermine. Their words are not known.

Descended from Garth Greenhand by his daughter Florys the Fox, House Florent boasts they have a superior claim to Highgarden than the Tyrells because of closer blood ties to House Gardener, the extinct Kings of the Reach.
facts: A red fox in a circle of blue flowers on ermine, (Ermine, a fox gules within an annulet of flowers azure)

footly.summary: House Footly of Tumbleton is a noble house from Tumbleton in the Reach. According to semi-canon sources, House Footly blazons their shields with a field of silver caltrops on black. Their motto is Tread Lightly Here.
facts: A field of silver caltrops on black, (Sable, semé of caltrops argent)

fossoway-of-cider-hall.summary:
House Fossoway of Cider Hall is a house of landed knights from the Reach, one of the principal bannermen sworn to House Tyrell. Cider Hall is located at the fork of the Mander and the Cockleswent. Their banner is a red apple over a golden field. Their words are "A Taste of Glory".

Formerly a lordly house, they are commonly referred as the red-apple Fossoways, to differentiate them from the green-apple Fossoways from New Barrel, the branch of the house that split from the red apples in 209 AC.
facts: A red apple on gold, (Or, an apple gules)
Knight of Cider Hall, Lord of Cider Hall (formerly)

fossoway-of-new-barrel.summary:
House Fossoway of New Barrel is a noble house from New Barrel in the Reach, sworn to House Tyrell of Highgarden.

They are commonly referred as the green-apple Fossoways to differentiate them from the original branch of the house, the red-apple Fossoways from Cider Hall.

Their banner is a green apple over a golden field. Their motto does not appear in the books.
facts: A green apple on gold, (Or, an apple vert)

fowler.summary:
House Fowler of Skyreach is a noble house from Skyreach in Dorne. They hold the title of "Warden of the Prince's Pass" and watch over the Prince's Pass.

Their words are "Let Me Soar". According to semi-canon sources their blazon is a hooded blue hawk on silver.
facts: A hooded blue hawk on silver, (Argent, a hooded hawk azure)
Lord of Skyreach, Warden of the Prince's Pass, Lord of the Wide Way, King of Stone and Sky (historical)

frey.summary:
House Frey of the Crossing is a noble house of the riverlands. Their main seat is the Twins, a pair of castles on each bank of the northern Green Fork of the Trident that serves as a vital bridge across the river. The lord of the house is called the Lord of the Crossing. Their sigil is two blue towers united by a bridge on silver-grey, representing the Twins. Their house words are not mentioned in the books.

The strategic location of the Twins has allowed the house to become quite wealthy, and House Frey rules over wider domains and can call upon more soldiers than their liege lords, House Tully of Riverrun. Under their current lord, Walder Frey, the family has continued to grow in both size and power, and they are now the most powerful bannermen of the Tullys.
facts: Two blue towers on silver-grey, (Cendrée, a bridge azure, at either end a tower of the same)

frey-of-riverrun.summary: House Frey of Riverrun is a new noble house in the riverlands, and is a cadet branch of House Frey of the Twins. It is created when House Tully is attainted of its lands and titles for rebellion against the Iron Throne. The lands are bestowed on Ser Emmon Frey, second son of Lord Walder Frey, and his wife Lady Genna Lannister.
facts: Two blue towers, united by a bridge, on a silver-grey field, (Cendrée, a bridge azure, at either end a tower of the same)

gardener.summary:
House Gardener of Highgarden is the extinct house of the old and famed Kings of the Reach. Beginning with the mythical first king Garth the Gardener, the Gardeners ruled, through war and peace and the assimilation with the Andals through the generations, until the last Gardener king, Mern IX Gardener, and his kin were killed at the Field of Fire in Aegon's Conquest.

The kings of House Gardener initially ruled the Reach proper, focused on Highgarden and the Mander river, but over time they used their claim of descending from Garth the Gardener to claim supremacy over neighboring kings and lords. Their seat was Highgarden, where many Gardener kings (and one queen) sat upon a living throne called the Oakenseat.

The Gardener kings wore crowns of vines and flowers when at peace, and crowns of bronze thorns (later iron) when they rode to war. Their blazon was a green hand over a white field, which inspired the chivalric Order of the Green Hand.
facts: A green hand on white, (Argent, a hand vert)
King of the Reach, Lord of Highgarden

gargalen.summary:
House Gargalen of Salt Shore is a major Dornish noble house. Their seat, Salt Shore, is located along the Summer Sea on the southern coast of Dorne.

Their blazon is a red cockatrice with black snake in beak on gold. Their words have not appeared on the books.
facts: A red cockatrice with black snake in beak on gold (Or, a cockatrice gules, in its beak a serpent sable)

glover.summary:
House Glover of Deepwood Motte is a noble house from the north, and is among the principal houses sworn to the Starks of Winterfell. Galbart Glover is the Master of Deepwood Motte, which is located in the northwestern wolfswood. Houses Bole, Branch, Forrester, and Woods of the wolfswood are sworn to the Glovers.

Their blazon is silver mailed fist on scarlet. Their words are not mentioned in the books.
facts: A silver fist on scarlet, (Gules, a mailed fist argent)

goodbrother.summary:
House Goodbrother of Hammerhorn is a noble house from the Iron Islands. They are one of the most powerful houses from Great Wyk, the largest of the islands, and are one of House Greyjoy's primary bannermen. Their keep of Hammerhorn is inland, in the Hardstone Hills, their wealth not coming from the Sunset Sea but from their mines.

Their blazon is a gold-banded black warhorn on red. Their motto has not appeared in the books.

House Goodbrother has at least three branches on Great Wyk, the Goodbrothers of Corpse Lake, the Goodbrothers of Crow Spike Keep, and the Goodbrothers of Downdelving. Other branches include the Goodbrothers of Shatterstone on Old Wyk and the Goodbrothers of Orkmont.
facts: A gold-banded black warhorn on red, (Gules, a warhorn sable banded or)
Lord of Hammerhorn, High King of the Iron Islands (historical)
House Goodbrother of Corpse Lake, House Goodbrother of Crow Spike Keep, House Goodbrother of Downdelving, House Goodbrother of Orkmont (possibly), House Goodbrother of Shatterstone (possibly)

grafton.summary:
House Grafton of Gulltown is a noble house from the Vale of Arryn, one of the main families sworn to House Arryn of the Eyrie. They rule over Gulltown, a main port and populated city, as well as the only city in the Vale.

They blazon their arms with a burning tower in yellow, within a black pile, upon flaming red.
facts: A burning tower in yellow, within a black pile, upon flaming red, (Gules, on a pile sable a tower or with flames issuant from the battlements)

greyjoy.summary: House Greyjoy of Pyke is one of the Great Houses of Westeros. They rule over the Iron Islands, a collection of isles off the west coast of Westeros, from the Seastone Chair in the castle of Pyke on the island of the same name. The head of the family is traditionally known as the Lord Reaper of Pyke. Their sigil is a golden kraken on a black field, and their house motto is "We Do Not Sow."
facts: A golden kraken on black, (Sable, a kraken or)
King of the Isles and the North, King of Salt and Rock, Son of the Sea Wind, Lord Reaper of Pyke, Lord of the Iron Islands (formerly), Prince of Winterfell (formerly)

grimm.summary:
House Grimm of Greyshield rules the island Greyshield, one of the Shield Islands of the Reach, from their castle, Grimston.

Neither their arms nor their words appear in the books, but according to semi-canon sources they blazon their shield as an iron escutcheon with silver studs on a grey-green field strewn with longships proper.
facts: An iron escutcheon with silver studs on a grey-green field strewn with longships proper, (Vert-cendrée semé of longships proper, an escutcheon cendrée platé)

harclay.summary:
House Harclay is one of the northern mountain clans in the north. They live in the hills to the north of the wolfswood.

According to semi-canon sources, they blazon their shield with three blue moons, waxing, full, waning, on a white bend, on blue.
facts: 3 blue moons, waxing, full, waning, on a white bend, on blue, (Azure, on a bend argent a hurt between an increscent and decrescent of the first)

harlaw.summary:
House Harlaw of Harlaw is one of the most powerful houses from the Iron Islands, sworn to House Greyjoy of Pyke. From the castle of Ten Towers, the Harlaws rule over the entire island of Harlaw, the richest and most populous of the isles. Their blazon is a silver scythe on black.

All the other houses on Harlaw pledge fealty to House Harlaw, including Houses Kenning, Myre, Stonetree, and Volmark. Branches of the Harlaws are located at Grey Garden, Harlaw Hall, Harridan Hill, and the Tower of Glimmering.
facts: A silver scythe on black, (Sable, a scythe argent)
Lord of Harlaw, Lord of Ten Towers, Harlaw of Harlaw, High King of the Iron Islands (historical)
Harlaws of Grey Garden, Harlaws of Harlaw Hall, Harlaws of Harridan Hill, Harlaws of the Tower of Glimmering

harlaw-of-grey-garden.summary: House Harlaw of Grey Garden is a branch of the main House Harlaw that rules the eponymous island from their seat at the Ten Towers. Their seat is Grey Garden.
facts: Quartered clockwise: a silver scythe on black, a peacock on cream, (Quarterly, 1st and 3rd sable, a scythe argent, 2nd and 4th carnation, a peacock in his pride proper)
Knight of Grey Garden, Lord of Greyshield

harlaw-of-harlaw-hall.summary: House Harlaw of Harlaw Hall is a cadet branch of the main House Harlaw that rules the eponymous island from their seat at the Ten Towers. Their seat is Harlaw Hall.
facts: Per bend black and silver, two scythes countercharged, (Per bend sable and argent, two scythes counterchanged)

harlaw-of-harridan-hill.summary: House Harlaw of Harridan Hill is a branch of the main House Harlaw that rules the eponymous island from their seat at the Ten Towers. Their seat is Harridan Hill.
facts: A silver scythe on pale blue, (Bleu celeste, a scythe argent)

harlaw-of-the-tower-of-glimmering.summary: House Harlaw of the Tower of Glimmering is a branch of the main House Harlaw that rules the eponymous island from their seat at the Ten Towers. The branch's seat is the Tower of Glimmering.
facts: A silver scythe on black within an embattled border, (Sable, a scythe within a bordure embattled argent)

hawick.summary: House Hawick of Saltpans is a noble house from Saltpans in the riverlands. Neither their arms nor their motto appear in the books. According to semi-canon sources, they blazon their arms with white sea birds strewn on a blue field.
facts: White sea birds strewn on a blue field, (Azure, semé of seabirds argent)

hayford.summary: House Hayford of Hayford is a noble house from Hayford in the crownlands, less than a day's ride from King's Landing. It is sworn directly to the Iron Throne. Their blazon is green fretty over gold, a green pale wavy.
facts: Green fretty over gold, a green pale wavy, (Or fretty vert, a pale wavy of the second)

hewett.summary:
House Hewett of Oakenshield rules over Oakenshield, one of the Shield Islands of the Reach.

They blazon their arms with an oaken escutcheon studded with iron, a field bendy of undulating blue and white. Their words are not mentioned in the books.
facts: An oaken escutcheon studded with iron, a field bendy of undulating blue and white, (Bendy undy azure and argent, an escutcheon brunâtre platé)

hightower.summary:
House Hightower of the Hightower, also known as House Hightower of Oldtown, is one of the most powerful of the noble houses in the Reach. Their seat is the Hightower, located in the city of Oldtown. The sigil of House Hightower is a stone white watchtower, with a fire on the top. Their motto is "We Light the Way", and they possess a Valyrian steel sword called Vigilance.

The Hightowers are among the oldest and proudest of the Great Houses. They have often preferred trade instead of war, and have also avoided many wars because of their support for the Faith of the Seven.

### Traits

A proud family, some Hightowers are said to have dabbled in alchemy and necromancy. Members of House Hightower thus far described tend to have silver or golden hair.
facts: A white tower topped with flames on smoke grey, (Cendrée, a tower argent, beacon inflamed gules)
Beacon of the South, Defender of Oldtown, Defender of the Citadel, Lord of Oldtown, Lord of the Hightower, Lord of the Port, Voice of Oldtown, King of the High Tower (historical)

hoare.summary:
House Hoare of Orkmont is an extinct house originally from the Iron Islands. Known as the black line, or the black blood, the Hoares became Kings of the Iron Islands after Andal settlers on the islands ended the rule of House Greyiron. While the Hoares originally came from Orkmont according to a semi-canon source, they also built Hoare Castle on Great Wyk. The Hoares eventually moved to Fairmarket and Harrenhal in the riverlands, where they ruled as Kings of the Isles and the Rivers for three generations.

According to semi-canon sources, the Hoare banner depicted per saltire and with two heavy silver chains crossing between a gold longship on black, a dark green pine on white, a cluster of red grapes on gold, and a black raven flying in a blue sky (clockwise). The sigil represented the distant lands that had been under the rule of the house: the longship for the Iron Islands, the pine for Bear Island, the grapes for the Arbor, and the raven for the maesters of Oldtown; all bound by the iron chains of the ironmen.
facts: King of the Iron Islands, King of the Isles and the Rivers

hornwood.summary:
House Hornwood of Hornwood is a noble house whose seat is Hornwood in the north. They are among the principal bannermen of Starks of Winterfell. Their sigil is a bull moose, brown on a field of dark orange. Their words are "Righteous in Wrath".

The lands of the House, which include the forest of the Hornwood and other castles beside Hornwood, border those of Houses Bolton and Manderly. The Hornwood lands extend west to the White Knife. Their ruler is known as the Lord of the Hornwood.
facts: A brown bullmoose with black antlers on orange, (Tenné, a bullmoose brunâtre attired sable)

hunter.summary:
House Hunter of Longbow Hall is one of the principal noble houses sworn to House Arryn. Their seat is Longbow Hall in the eastern Vale.

According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with five silver arrows, fanned, on brown. Their motto does not appear in the books.
facts: Five silver arrows, fanned, on brown, (Brunâtre, a sheaf of five arrows, points to chief, argent)

jordayne.summary:
House Jordayne of the Tor is one of the principal noble houses of Dorne. The Tor is situated on the southern coast of the Sea of Dorne.

Their blazon is a golden quill on checkered dark and light green. Their words do not appear in the books, but in a semi-canon source they are stated to be "Let it be Written".
facts: A golden quill on checkered dark and light green, (Chequy vert and vert of a paler variety, a quill or)

karstark.summary: House Karstark of Karhold is a noble house from Karhold in the north. They were founded as a branch of their overlords, the Starks of Winterfell, and are among their principal bannermen. The Karstark blazon is a white sunburst on black and their motto is "The Sun of Winter".
facts: A white sunburst on black, (Sable, a sunburst argent)
House Stark of Karhold: more than a thousand years ago (before 700 BC), House Karstark of Karhold: "over the centuries"

kenning-of-kayce.summary:
House Kenning of Kayce is a noble house from the westerlands. They blazon their arms with four sunbursts counterchanged on quartered orange and black.

The Kennings may have been landed knights at their origin and gained a lordly status at some time after the Dance of the Dragons, since their rulers have used the title Knight of Kayce in the past.
facts: Four sunbursts countercharged on quartered orange and black, (Quarterly tenné and sable, four suns-in-splendour counterchanged)
Lord of Kayce, Knight of Kayce (formerly)

knott.summary:
House Knott is a mountain clan in the north. In Winterfell, the head of the mountain clan are addressed by the title "Lord Knott" but their clan folk call them "The Knott".

The clan lives in the hills and mountains north of the wolfswood.
facts: A brown fret on white, (Argent, a fret brunâtre)

lannister.summary:
House Lannister of Casterly Rock is one of the Great Houses of Seven Kingdoms, and the principal house of the westerlands. Their seat is Casterly Rock, though another branch exists in nearby Lannisport. Their sigil is a golden roaring lion on a field of crimson. Their official motto is "Hear Me Roar!" However, their unofficial motto, equally well known, is "A Lannister always pays his debts." The Warden of the West is a Lannister by tradition. Their gold mines have made the Lannisters the wealthiest of the Great Houses, and the Lannister fleet is anchored at Lannisport.

Through the female line the Lannisters boast of descent from Lann the Clever, the legendary trickster of the Age of Heroes who tricked the members of House Casterly into giving him Casterly Rock during the era of the First Men. Later marrying Andals, the Lannisters reigned as Kings of the Rock until the Targaryen conquest, when they were defeated at the Field of Fire. King Loren I Lannister's surrender to Aegon the Conqueror allowed the Lannisters to remain the liege lords of the westerlands.

The current Lord of Casterly Rock is Tywin Lannister, whose daughter Cersei is the queen of King Robert I Baratheon, while her twin, Ser Jaime, is a knight of Robert's Kingsguard. Tywin's youngest child is Tyrion, a dwarf.
facts: A roaring lion, gold on crimson, (Gules, a lion or)
Lord of Casterly Rock, Shield of Lannisport, Warden of the West, King of the Rock (historical)
House Lannister of Lannisport, House Lannister of Darry, House Lannett (possibly), House Lanny (possibly), House Lantell (possibly)

lannister-of-darry.summary: House Lannister of Darry is a newly-created noble house from Castle Darry in the riverlands, and a branch of House Lannister of Casterly Rock. The House's sigil is the lion of Lannister, gold on red, quartered with the Darry plowman.
facts: Quarterly clockwise, a gold lion on a crimson field; a black plowman on a brown field, (Quarterly, first and third gules, a lion or, second and fourth brunâtre, a plowman sable)

lefford.summary:
House Lefford of the Golden Tooth is one of the principal houses sworn to House Lannister of Casterly Rock. The seat of the House is the Golden Tooth. The castle controls the main entrance to the westerlands from the east.

House Lefford blazons its arms with a golden inverted pile on sky blue, a sun left in the sky.
facts: A golden inverted pile on sky blue, a yellow sun in the first, (Bleu celeste, a pile reversed golden, in canton a sun-in-splendor yellow)

liddle.summary:
House Liddle is the formal name given to the Liddles, one of the northern mountain clans in the north. They inhabit the high mountains north of the wolfswood. The chief of the clan is known as "The Liddle", although at Winterfell he is given the treatment of "Lord Liddle".

Their arms are per pale white and green, a fir tree line between, three brown pinecones on the white. Their motto does not appear in the books.
facts: Per pale white and green, a fir tree line between, three brown pinecones on the white, (Per pale sapiné argent and vert, in dexter three pinecones brunâtre)

locke.summary:
House Locke of Oldcastle is a noble house from Oldcastle in the north.

Their banner is two bronze keys crossed on a white pale on purple. Their words do not appear in the text.
facts: Bronze crossed keys on a white pale on purple, (Purpure, on a pale argent two keys saltirewise bronze)

lychester.summary: House Lychester is a noble house in the riverlands. They own a small square keep. According to semi-canon sources, they blazon their arms with orange and white gyronny, a black talon.
facts: Orange and white gyronny, a black talon, (Gyronny tenné and argent, an eagle's leg erased sable)

lydden.summary:
House Lydden of the Deep Den is one of the main noble houses of the westerlands. Their castle, the Deep Den, is located on the Goldroad south of Hornvale and north of Silverhill.

Their banner is a white badger on per pale green and brown. Their motto has not been mentioned.
facts: A white badger on per pale green and brown, (Per pale vert and brunâtre, a badger argent)

lynderly.summary:
House Lynderly of the Snakewood is a noble house from the Vale of Arryn. Their castle is Snakewood and they carry the title "Lord of the Snakewood".

They blazon their arms with a black field strewn with wriggling green serpents.
facts: A black field strewn wriggling green serpents, (Sable, semé of snakes vert)

magnar.summary: House Magnar of Kingshouse is a noble house from Kingshouse on the island of Skagos in the north. According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with a green lobster on white, its claws holding a black harpoon. Their name derives from magnar, an Old Tongue word meaning "lord".
facts: A green lobster on white, its claws holding a black harpoon, (Argent, a lobster vert holding a harpoon sable)

mallister.summary:
House Mallister of Seagard is one of the most prominent noble houses from the riverlands. Seagard is a fortress built to defend the coast against the reavers from the Iron Islands, and dates from before Aegon's Conquest.

Their blazon is a silver eagle displayed, on a purple field. Their motto is "Above the rest".
facts: A silver eagle displayed on indigo, (Purpure, an eagle displayed argent)
Lord of Seagard, King of the Trident (historical)

manderly.summary:
House Manderly of White Harbor is a noble family in the north whose seat is the New Castle in the city of White Harbor. Their blazon is a white merman with dark green hair, beard and tail, carrying a black trident, over a blue-green field. Their words do not appear in the books, nor has George R. R. Martin submitted them in semi-canon material.

The Manderlys originated from Dunstonbury in the Reach, but were forced into exile by House Gardener. The Kings of Winter, House Stark of Winterfell, accepted the Manderlys in the north and granted them the Wolf's Den, where the newcomers developed the prosperous city of White Harbor.

The Lord of White Harbor, Wyman Manderly, claims to influence all lands and houses east of the mouth of the White Knife, including Houses Locke, Woolfield, and Flint of Widow's Watch. The Manderlys' dominion includes the Sheepshead Hills and the Broken Branch, as well as the allegiance of Ramsgate. Their bannermen includes a dozen petty lords and a hundred landed knights.
facts: A white merman with dark green hair, beard and tail, carrying a black trident, on a blue-green field, (Aquamarine, a merman argent crined, bearded and queued vert, carrying a trident sable)
Lord of White Harbor, Warden of the White Knife, Shield of the Faith, Defender of the Dispossessed, Lord Marshal of the Mander, Knight of the Order of the Green Hand, Lord of Dunstonbury (formerly)

manwoody.summary:
House Manwoody of Kingsgrave is a noble house from Kingsgrave in northern Dorne. Their seat is placed amidst the Prince's Pass, guarding access to Dorne.

The Manwoodys blazon their banners with a white skull with a golden crown, over a black field. Their motto has not been mentioned in the books.
facts: A white skull crowned with gold on black, (Sable, a skull argent crowned or)

marbrand.summary:
House Marbrand of Ashemark is one of the main noble houses of the westerlands. Their seat of Ashemark is located in the hilly area near where the Tumblestone begins.

Their blazon is a burning tree, orange on smoke. Their motto does not appear in the books, but according to a semi-canon source it is "Burning Bright".
facts: A burning tree, orange on smoke, (Cendrée, a tree tenné in flame)

martell.summary:
House Nymeros Martell of Sunspear, usually simply called House Martell, is one of the Great Houses of the Seven Kingdoms and the ruling house of Dorne. "Nymeros" indicates "of the line of Nymeria," referring to the union of the Martells with the Rhoynish warrior queen Nymeria around 700 BC. The Prince of Dorne rules from Sunspear in southeastern Dorne, and the family also watches over the shadow city, the Planky Town, and the Water Gardens.

The Martells of old used a spear as their emblem, while Nymeria and her Rhoynar used the sun as theirs. When Nymeria wed Lord Mors Martell, the symbols were combined into a gold spear piercing a red sun on an orange field. Their words are Unbowed, Unbent, Unbroken.
facts: Lord of Sunspear, Lord of the Sandship (formerly), Prince of Dorne
Coming of the Andals (House Martell of the Sandship), ~ 700 BC (House Nymeros Martell of Sunspear)

massey.summary: House Massey of Stonedance is a noble house from Stonedance on Massey's Hook in the crownlands. They blazon their arms with a triple spiral; red, green and blue, on white, an ancient sigil for an ancient House.
facts: A triple spiral; red, green and blue, on white, (Argent, a triple gurges gules, vert and azure)

meadows.summary:
House Meadows of Grassy Vale is a noble house from the Reach. Their castle is Grassfield Keep in or near the town of Grassy Vale. They are sworn to House Tyrell of Highgarden.

According to semi-canon sources, House Meadows blazons their shield with a border of flowers of many colors and varieties on green.
facts: A border of flowers of many colors and varieties on green, (Vert, an orle of flowers variegated)

melcolm.summary: House Melcolm of Old Anchor is a noble house from Old Anchor in the Vale of Arryn. It is one of the principal houses sworn to House Arryn. According to semi-canon sources, they blazon their arms with a rusty anchor on turquoise beneath yellow chief with three blue plates.
facts: A rusty anchor on turquoise beneath yellow chief with three blue plates, (Aquamarine, a rusted anchor, on a chief or three hurts)

merryweather.summary:
House Merryweather of Longtable is a noble house from the Reach. Their seat of Longtable is located at the confluence of the Mander and the Blueburn. Historically a prominent family of the Reach, House Merryweather has lost lands and wealth after Robert's Rebellion.

Their blazon is a golden horn of plenty spilling out apples, carrots, plums, onions, leeks, turnips, and fruits of many colors, over a white field bordered in gold. Their motto is "Behold our Bounty."

mertyns.summary: House Mertyns of Mistwood is a noble house from Mistwood in the stormlands, sworn to House Baratheon. They blazon their arms with a white great horned owl on grey. Their words are not known.
facts: A white great horned owl on grey, (Cendrée, a great-horned-owl argent)

mooton.summary:
House Mooton of Maidenpool is a noble house from the riverlands. Their seat of Maidenpool is one of the main ports and trade centers of the Bay of Crabs.

Their blazon is a red salmon on white, over a white field with a golden tressure. According to semi-canon sources their motto is "Wisdom and Strength".

House Mooton is historically far wealthier than their liege lords, House Tully of Riverrun.
facts: A red salmon on white, a gold tressure, (Argent, a salmon gules within a tressure or)
Lord of Maidenpool, King (in the Age of Heroes)
Before the coming of the Andals

mormont.summary:
House Mormont of Bear Island is a noble house of the north, one of the principal families sworn to House Stark. Their seat is at Bear Island, located in the Bay of Ice northwest of Winterfell. Their blazon is a black bear over a green wood and their motto is "Here We Stand".

House Mormont is one of the few houses to have an ancestral weapon of Valyrian steel: a bastard sword called Longclaw. However, due to Bear Island's lack of valuable resources, the Mormonts are a rather poor house. Their hall is made of huge logs, surrounded by an earthen palisade. On the gate is a carving of a woman in a bearskin with a child in one arm suckling at her breast and a battleaxe in the other.
facts: A black bear in a green wood, (Barry sapiné vert and vert of a paler variety, a bear sable)
Longclaw (formerly; now gifted to Jon Snow)

morrigen.summary:
House Morrigen of Crow's Nest is a noble house from Crow's Nest in the stormlands.

Their arms are a black crow in flight on storm-green. Their motto does not appear in the books.
facts: A black crow in flight on storm-green, (Vert, a crow volant sable)

mullendore.summary:
House Mullendore of Uplands is one of the principal noble houses from the Reach. Their seat, Uplands, is east of Oldtown. They are sworn to the Hightowers.

Their arms depict a field of black-and-orange butterflies strewn over white. Their motto does not appear in the books.
facts: Black-and-orange butterflies on white, (Argent, semé of butterflies sable and tenné)

norrey.summary:
House Norrey is the formal name given to the Norreys, a mountain clan from the north that inhabits the high mountains north of the wolfswood. Of the mountain clans, the Norreys live closest to the Gift. The chief of the clan is known as "The Norrey", although at Winterfell he is given the treatment of "Lord Norrey".

Their arms do not appear in the book, but according to semi-canon sources, they blazon their banners with six green thistles over a yellow field.
facts: Six green thistles, 3-2-1, on yellow, (Or, six thistles 3-2-1 vert)

oakheart.summary:
House Oakheart of Old Oak is an old and powerful family from Old Oak in the Reach, one of the main houses sworn to House Tyrell. They are among the noble houses from the Reach that can trace their descent from Garth Greenhand.

Their arms are three green oak leaves on gold. Their banner is thus referred to as the Three Leaves. According to semi-canon sources, their motto is "Our Roots Go Deep".
facts: Three green oak leaves on gold, (Or, three oak leaves vert)
Lord of Old Oak, King (in the Age of Heroes)

orkwood.summary:
House Orkwood of Orkmont is a noble house from the Iron Islands, with their seat being on the island of Orkmont.

They blazon their arms as dark green pines strewn closely together on yellow.
facts: Dark green pines strewn closely together on yellow, (Or semé of pines vert)

osgrey.summary:
House Osgrey of Standfast is a noble house from Standfast in the Reach. Sworn to House Rowan of Goldengrove, its lands border those of House Webber and House Stackhouse. They once were among the greatest houses of the Reach, with four castles. However, by 211 AC, they had not been lords in centuries, and were only landed knights with a single towerhouse. The Osgrey fortunes improved in that year, but their status is unknown afterwards.

House Osgrey had at least one cadet branch at Leafy Lake, but by 211 AC they had become extinct.

Their blazon is a chequy lion, green and gold rampant on a field of white. Their motto has not appeared yet.
facts: A lion, checkered green and gold, on white, (Argent, a lion chequy vert and or)
Knight of Standfast, Lord of Coldmoat (formerly), Marshal of the Northmarch (pre-Conquest)

peake.summary:
House Peake of Starpike is a noble house from Starpike in the Reach. They blazon their arms with three black castles on orange. The three black castles on their arms symbolize the three castles that House Peake once owned: Starpike, Dunstonbury, and Whitegrove. Since they gained Dunstonbury after having driven the Manderlys from the Reach at the behest of House Gardener, their arms were presumably different before this. Their motto has yet to appear.

The Peakes are Marcher lords from the Dornish Marches. According to Archmaester Gyldayn, House Peake was "land poor, rich in stone and soil and pride, yet chronically short of coin" during the rule of Lord Unwin Peake.
facts: Three black castles on orange, (Tenné, three castles sable)
Lord of Starpike, Lord of Dunstonbury (formerly), Lord of Whitegrove (formerly)

piper.summary:
House Piper of Pinkmaiden is one of the chief noble houses from the riverlands. Its seat at Pinkmaiden Castle is located on the Red Fork close to the border with the westerlands.

Their blazon is a pink dancing maiden in a swirl of white silk, over blue. Their motto is not mentioned in the books, but in semi-canon sources it is listed as "Brave and Beautiful".
facts: A dancing maiden pink in a swirl of white silk, on blue, (Azure, a maiden dancing carnation enwrapped with silk argent)

prester.summary:
House Prester of Feastfires is one of the principal noble houses sworn to House Lannister of Casterly Rock. Their seat at Feastfires is located at the westernmost point of the westerlands.

Their blazon is a red ox on ermine. Their motto is not mentioned in the books, but according to semi-canon sources it is "Tireless".
facts: A red ox on ermine, (Ermine, an ox gules)

pryor.summary: House Pryor of Pebble is a noble house from Pebble in the Vale. According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with a partial eclipse, black moon over yellow sun, on dusty pink.
facts: A partial eclipse, black moon over yellow sun, on dusty pink, (Rose, a sun-in-splendour or partially surmounted by a moon in her complement sable)

qorgyle.summary:
House Qorgyle of Sandstone is a noble house from Sandstone, located in the dunes of western Dorne. They are among the principal bannermen sworn to House Martell of Sunspear.

Their arms are three black scorpions over red.
facts: Three black scorpions on red, (Gules, three scorpions sable)

redfort.summary: House Redfort of Redfort is one of the principal noble houses in the Vale of Arryn. They blazon their arms with a red castle on a white field within a red embattled border. Their motto does not appear in the books, but according to semi-canon sources it is As Strong as Stone.
facts: A red castle on a white field within a red embattled border, (Argent, a castle within a bordure embattled gules)

redwyne.summary:
House Redwyne of the Arbor is one of the main noble houses sworn to Highgarden. Their seat is the Arbor, an island located off the southwestern-most part of Westeros, known for making the best wines in Westeros. The Redwynes control the Redwyne fleet, the largest fleet in Westeros, containing two hundred warships and five times as many merchant carracks, wine cogs, trading galleys, and whalers.

The sigil of House Redwyne is a burgundy grape cluster on blue, symbolizing the famed wines of the Arbor. Their words are not known.

The current Lord of the Arbor, Paxter Redwyne, is married to his cousin, Mina Tyrell, the sister of his liege, Lord Mace Tyrell. Paxter's elderly aunt, Lady Olenna Redwyne, the "Queen of Thorns", is the mother of Mace and Mina.
facts: A burgundy grape cluster on blue, (Azure, a grape-cluster murrey)
Lord of the Arbor, King of the Arbor (historical)

reed.summary:
House Reed of Greywater Watch is a noble house from Greywater Watch, and one of the principal families in the north. They rule the crannogmen, small men who live in the swamps and marshes of the Neck.

According to semi-canon sources their arms are a black lizard-lion on grey-green. Their motto does not appear in the books.
facts: A black lizard-lion on grey-green, (Vert-cendrée, a lizard-lion sable)

roote.summary: House Roote of Lord Harroway's Town is a noble house from Harroway in the riverlands. According to semi-canon sources, they blazon their arms with a two-headed horse, brown, on a field of wavy green and green. They may have taken their sigil from Old King Andahar, as the ferry boat at Harroway is referred to as the king's two-headed water horse.
facts: A two-headed horse, brown, on a field of wavy green and green, (Wavy vert and vert, a horse bicapitated brunâtre)

rosby.summary:
House Rosby of Rosby is a noble house from the crownlands. They rule the castle of Rosby and its village, which are located just northeast of King's Landing. The Rosbys are not known for their robustness.

Their blazon consists into three red chevronels on ermine. Their motto is not mentioned in the books.
facts: Three red chevronels on ermine, (Ermine, three chevronels inverted gules)

rowan.summary:
House Rowan of Goldengrove is one of the most prominent and old families from the Reach, its dominions extending all along its northern borders. This may mean that the Rowans were made Marshal of the Northmarch to replace the declining House Osgrey, now their bannermen. Their blazon is a golden tree on silver. Their words are not mentioned in the books.

Like several other major Reach houses, the Rowans can trace their descent from the legendary Garth Greenhand, through his daughter Rowan Gold-Tree.
facts: A golden tree on silver, (Argent, a tree or)
Lord of Goldengrove, Marshal of the Northmarch (possibly)

royce.summary:
House Royce of Runestone is an old and powerful noble house of the Vale, sworn to House Arryn. Their seat is the castle Runestone, located on the coast of the narrow sea north of Gulltown. There is also a junior branch occupying the non-hereditary seat of the Gates of the Moon, located on the path that leads to the Eyrie.

The Royces of Runestone blazon their arms with black iron studs on bronze, bordered with runes, and their motto is "We Remember".
facts: Black iron studs on bronze, bordered with rune, (Bronze pelleté, a bordure of ancient runes)
Lord of Runestone, High King of the Vale, the Fingers and the Mountains of the Moon (historical), Bronze King (historical)

royce-of-the-gates-of-the-moon.summary: House Royce of the Gates of the Moon is a noble house from the Gates of the Moon in the Vale of Arryn. They began as a junior branch of House Royce of Runestone. According to semi-canon sources, they blazon their arms with a black portcullis over a white crescent moon on purple bordered with runes on bronze. Their motto has not appeared yet.

ryger.summary: House Ryger of Willow Wood is a noble house from Willow Wood in the riverlands. It is one of the main houses sworn to House Tully. They blazon their arms with a weeping willow, green on white.
facts: A weeping willow, green on white, (Argent, a willow-tree vert)

saltcliffe.summary:
House Saltcliffe of Saltcliffe is one of the ironborn noble houses on the island of Saltcliffe in the Iron Islands. According to a semi-canon source, the Saltcliffes rule the isle and are named after it.

According to semi-canon sources their sigil is a nine-headed serpent, black on silver. Their words are not mentioned in the books.
facts: A nine-headed serpent, black on silver, (Argent, a serpent nine-headed sable)

santagar.summary:
House Santagar of Spottswood is a house of landed knights from Spottswood in Dorne. They are one of the main houses sworn to Sunspear.

Neither their arms or their motto appear in the books. In a semi-canon source they blazon their arms with a spotted leopard with a golden axe, over a per bend sinister blue and white field.
facts: Per bend sinister blue and white, a spotted leopard with golden axe, (Per bend sinister azure and argent, a spotted-leopard proper bearing an axe or)

sarsfield.summary: House Sarsfield of Sarsfield is a noble house from Sarsfield in the westerlands. It blazons its shield with a green arrow on a white bend on green. According to semi-canon sources, their motto is "True to the Mark".
facts: A green arrow on white bend on green, (Vert, on a bend argent an arrow of the field)

selmy.summary: ­House Selmy of Harvest Hall is one of the principal noble houses from the Stormlands. Among the greatest marcher lords, their seat is Harvest Hall in the Dornish Marches. The Selmys blazon their arms with three stalks of yellow wheat on brown.
facts: Three stalks of yellow wheat on brown, (Brunâtre, three stalks of wheat or)

serrett.summary:
House Serrett of Silverhill is a noble house from Silverhill in the westerlands. They are one of the principal houses sworn to House Lannister of Casterly Rock.

They blazon their arms with a peacock in his pride on cream. Their words according to semi-canon sources are "I Have No Rival".
facts: A peacock in his pride on cream, (Carnation, a peacock in his pride proper)

serry.summary:
House Serry of Southshield rules over Southshield, the southernmost of the Shield Islands of the Reach.

Their blazon is a white rose upon a red escutcheon upon white, within a red embattled border. Their motto has not appeared in the books.
facts: A white rose upon a red escutcheon upon white, a red embattled border, (Argent, an escutcheon gules charged with a rose of the first all within a bordure embattled of the second)

shett-of-gulltown.summary:
House Shett of Gulltown is a branch of House Shett from Gulltown in the Vale of Arryn. The Shetts of Gulltown are probably landed knights, since House Grafton holds the title of Lord of Gulltown.

According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with nine white seagulls on a field of brown.
facts: Nine white seagulls on a field of brown, (Brunâtre, nine seagulls proper)

slynt.summary: House Slynt of Harrenhal is a noble house from Harrenhal in the riverlands. Originating from King's Landing in the crownlands, their blazon is a bloody spear, gold on a field of night-black, with a border of checkered gold and black. The motto of the house is not mentioned.
facts: A bloody spear, gold on black, with a border of checkered gold and black, (Sable, a spear or tipped sanguine, a bordure chequy or and sable)

smallwood.summary:
House Smallwood of Acorn Hall is a noble house from Acorn Hall in the riverlands. Their sigil is six brown acorns on yellow. According to semi-canon sources, their motto is "From These Beginnings".

Though formerly sworn directly to House Tully, the Smallwoods are now vassals of House Vance, but it is not confirmed if this is House Vance of Atranta or House Vance of Wayfarer's Rest.

The lands of House Smallwood are near those that belonged to House Goodbrook.
facts: Six brown acorns, 3-2-1, on yellow, (Or, six acorns 3-2-1 brunâtre)

sparr.summary:
House Sparr of Great Wyk is an ironborn noble house on the island of Great Wyk in the Iron Islands. Their lands are about six leagues from Hammerhorn. House Sparr's lord is known as the Sparr.

According to semi-canon sources House Sparr blazon their arms with oak saltire on blue.
facts: Oak saltire on blue, (Azure, a saltire brunâtre)

spicer.summary: House Spicer is a minor noble house of the westerlands. They blazon their arms with three black pepperpots on a saffron bend, across a field of green and silver stripes.
facts: 3 pepperpots on a saffron bend, upon green and silver stripes, (Paly vert and argent, three pepperpots proper on a bend tenné)

stane.summary: House Stane of Driftwood Hall is a noble house from Driftwood Hall on the isle of Skagos in the north. According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with a driftwood tree, bare and brown, on pale green.
facts: A driftwood tree, bare and brown, on pale green, (Vert, a driftwood tree blasted brunâtre)

stark.summary:
House Stark of Winterfell is one of the Great Houses of Westeros and the principal noble house of the north. In days of old they ruled as Kings of Winter, but since Aegon's Conquest they have been Wardens of the North and ruled as Lords of Winterfell. Their seat, Winterfell, is an ancient castle renowned for its strength.

Their sigil is a grey direwolf racing across a field of white. Their words are "Winter Is Coming", one of only a few house mottoes to be a warning rather than a boast. Several of the POV characters of A Song of Ice and Fire are members of House Stark.

Aside from the Karstarks of Karhold, the Starks of Winterfell may have other, distant relatives in the north. White Harbor and Barrowton are considered to be likely options for offshoot branches. Some younger Starks have also held vassal holdfasts for the Lords of Winterfell.
facts: A running grey direwolf, on an ice-white field, (Argent, a direwolf courant cendrée)
King of Winter/King in the North (formerly), Prince of Winterfell (formerly), Lord of Winterfell (formerly), Warden of the North (formerly), King of the Trident (formerly)
Rickon Stark (Bran's heir), Jon Snow (per Robb Stark's will)
House Greystark (extinct), House Karstark, Barrowton Starks (possibly), White Harbor Starks (possibly)

staunton.summary: House Staunton of Rook's Rest is a noble house from Rook's Rest in the crownlands. Neither their arms nor their motto have appeared in the books, but according to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with two black wings upon a white fess on checkered black and grey.
facts: Two black wings upon a white fess on checkered black and grey, (Chequy sable and cendrée, on a fess argent two wings of the first)

stokeworth.summary:
House Stokeworth of Stokeworth is a noble house from the crownlands. Sworn directly to King's Landing, they live at nearby Castle Stokeworth north of the capital.

They blazon their arms with a white lamb holding a golden goblet on a green field. Their motto is "Proud to be Faithful".
facts: A white lamb holding a golden goblet on a green field, (Vert, a lamb proper holding a goblet or)

stonehouse.summary:
House Stonehouse of Old Wyk is a noble house from Old Wyk, one of the Iron Islands. They are one of the main houses sworn to Pyke.

Neither their arms or their motto appear in the books. According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with a black brazier on a grey masonry field.
facts: A black brazier on a grey masonry field, (Cendrée masoned proper, a brazier sable)

stout.summary: House Stout of Goldgrass is a petty noble house from the north who have a modest keep near the eastern gate of Barrowton. It is sworn to House Dustin. According to semi-canon sources, they blazon their arms as chevronny russet and gold and their seat is named Goldgrass.
facts: Chevronny russet and gold, (Chevronny inverted brunâtre and or)

sunderland.summary:
House Sunderland of the Three Sisters rules the Three Sisters, islands located in the Bite. The Sunderlands are sworn to House Arryn of the Eyrie.

House Sunderland blazons their arms with three women's heads, white with black hair, on barry wavy blue and green. Their motto does not appear in the books. The name of their seat, possibly located on Sweetsister, is as yet unknown.
facts: Three women's heads, white with black hair, on blue and green undy, (Barry wavy azure and vert, three women's heads argents, crined sable)
Lord of the Three Sisters, King of the Three Sisters (historical)

sunderly.summary:
House Sunderly of Saltcliffe is one of the main nobles houses from the Iron Islands. Their seat is located on the island of Saltcliffe.

Neither their arms or their motto appear in the books. According to semi-canon sources they blazon their arms with a drowned man, pink and pale, floating upright in a blue-green sea, his hair streaming upwards, as fish nibble at his limbs.

sunglass.summary:
House Sunglass of Sweetport Sound is a noble house sworn to Dragonstone. The location of Sweetport Sound in the crownlands has not been stated.

Their blazon is composed by seven golden seven-pointed stars in a ring on white. Their motto does not appear in the books.
facts: Seven golden seven-pointed stars in a ring on white, (Argent, seven mullets of seven points or)

swann.summary: House Swann of Stonehelm is one of the primary noble houses of the stormlands. They are marcher lords ruling from Stonehelm over the lands surrounding the Red Watch on Cape Wrath in the eastern Dornish Marches. They blazon their arms with argent and sable a swan counter charged.
facts: Battling swans black and white, beaks and feet golden, on per pale white and black, (Per pale argent and sable, two swans combatant counterchanged, beaked and membered or)

swyft.summary:
House Swyft of Cornfield is a knightly house from Cornfield in the westerlands. They are among the principal houses sworn to House Lannister of Casterly Rock.

Their arms depict a blue bantam rooster on yellow. According to semi-canon sources, their words are "Awake! Awake!".
facts: A blue bantam rooster on yellow, (Or, a cock azure)
Knight of Cornfield, Lord of Cornfield (formerly)

tallhart.summary:
House Tallhart of Torrhen's Square is a noble house from the north and is among the principal houses sworn to House Stark. Ser Helman Tallhart is the Master of Torrhen's Square, which is located southwest of Winterfell.

Their arms show three green sentinel trees, over a brown field. The words of the house do not appear in the books, but according to a semi-canon source they are "Proud and Free".
facts: Three sentinel trees, green on brown, (Brunâtre, three sentinel trees vert)

targaryen.summary:
House Targaryen of King's Landing is a noble family of Valyrian descent who once ruled the Seven Kingdoms of Westeros. The Targaryen sigil is a red three-headed dragon, breathing red flames on black. The house words are "Fire and Blood".

The only family of dragonlords who survived the Doom of Valyria, the Targaryens left the Valyrian Freehold twelve years before the Doom. They resided for more than a century at Dragonstone castle on Dragonstone island, until Aegon the Conqueror and his sister-wives, Visenya and Rhaenys, began the first of the Wars of Conquest in 2 BC.

During Aegon's Conquest, the family built the Aegonfort in the new capital city of King's Landing. The Aegonfort was later torn down and replaced by the Red Keep, which remained their main seat for the duration of their dynasty, and which housed the Iron Throne. Their original castle was almost always given to the heir to the throne, the Prince of Dragonstone. The Targaryens eventually built the summer residence Summerhall, which has been given to several younger sons of the family over time.

House Targaryen ruled as the Kings of the Andals, the Rhoynar, and the First Men, the Lords of the Seven Kingdoms, and the Great House of the crownlands for nearly three hundred years. Seventeen male Targaryens ruled from the Iron Throne. The dynasty ended with the death of Aerys the Mad King during Robert's Rebellion, in which the Targaryens were overthrown and replaced by House Baratheon.
